overview: The Blue Revolution – Neela Kranti scheme, launched in 2015-16 and running until 2019-20, was a centrally sponsored initiative by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, with a central outlay of ₹3,000 crore that helped mobilize a total investment of ₹5,000 crore. It laid the foundation for integrated fisheries development by focusing on increasing fish production and productivity through technological upgradation, expansion of aquaculture, and development of fisheries infrastructure. The scheme aimed to enhance the socio-economic conditions of fishers and fish farmers while promoting sustainable and responsible utilization of fisheries resources.
objectives: Increase fish production and productivity through technological upgradation and expansion of aquaculture
Enhance the socio-economic conditions of fishers and fish farmers
Promote sustainable and responsible utilization of fisheries resources
Develop fisheries infrastructure including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, and aquaculture facilities
Strengthen the fisheries value chain through post-harvest infrastructure and market linkages
Encourage private investment and entrepreneurship in the fisheries sector
Improve fish quality and safety through better handling and processing practices
Generate employment opportunities in the fisheries and aquaculture sectors
eligibility: The scheme was open to State Governments, Union Territories, fisheries cooperatives, fish farmers, entrepreneurs, and other stakeholders involved in fisheries and aquaculture activities. Beneficiaries had to submit project proposals through the respective State Fisheries Departments for approval and funding under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme framework. Specific eligibility criteria varied by component but generally required adherence to scheme guidelines, technical feasibility, and financial viability of proposed projects.
benefits: The scheme provided financial assistance for the development of fisheries infrastructure, including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, aquaculture farms, hatcheries, and post-harvest facilities. It supported technological upgradation, capacity building, and training for fishers and entrepreneurs. It facilitated access to credit and subsidies for inputs such as seed, feed, and equipment. The scheme also promoted market linkages, value addition, and export-oriented activities. Additionally, it contributed to employment generation, livelihood diversification, and improved socio-economic conditions for coastal and inland fishing communities.
financial_support: The Blue Revolution Scheme had a central outlay of ₹3,000 crore, which helped mobilize a total investment of ₹5,000 crore. Financial support was provided as a subsidy through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) mechanism, where the Government of India provided grant-in-aid to State Governments and Union Territories for implementing approved projects. The funding pattern typically followed a 60:40 ratio (Central:State) for general States and 90:10 for Himalayan and North-Eastern States, with 100% central funding for Union Territories. Funds were released in installments based on project progress and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Identify the project component under Blue Revolution Scheme (e.g., aquaculture development, infrastructure, post-harvest). 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) as per scheme guidelines. 3. Submit the DPR to the respective State Fisheries Department. 4. State Fisheries Department forwards the proposal to the Department of Fisheries, Government of India for appraisal and approval. 5. Upon approval, obtain sanction letter and proceed with project implementation. 6. Utilize funds as per approved plan and submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates. 7. Claim reimbursement or receive funds in installments based on milestone achievement.
required_documents: No Objection Certificate (NOC) from relevant authorities
deadlines: The scheme operated from 2015-16 to 2019-20. Applications were accepted during the scheme period based on annual budget allocations and State-level proposals. There was no fixed rolling deadline; submissions were invited periodically as per scheme guidelines and fund availability.
implementing_agency: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India
caveats: The scheme was limited to the period 2015-16 to 2019-20 and is no longer accepting new applications.
Funding was subject to availability of budget and approval of project proposals by the Department of Fisheries.
Beneficiaries had to adhere to scheme-specific guidelines and submit utilization certificates for fund release.
Projects had to be completed within the stipulated timeline; delays could affect fund disbursement.
The scheme has been subsumed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) launched in 2020-21.
